Date: 2026-03-08
Time: 15:00 UTC

Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Maya Lin (Head of ML - Seastar), Carlos Vega (CTO - Seastar), Ethan Park (Eng Manager - Seastar)
summary: Initial integration discovery for Seastar Commerce evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main topics: SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain/LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy options, rate limits/quotas, observability hooks and audit logs, security (SOC 2, KMS), pricing/throughput tradeoffs. Customer concerned about latency for search ranking use-case and data residency. Agreed next steps: pricing, security docs, technical deep dive for private/VPC, sample LangChain notebook.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Security: SOC2, KMS, audit logs, SSO
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan from Redwood, and with me is Priya our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Maya: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting us in. We're exploring hosted vs dedicated vs private for a new ranking and search product.
[00:16] Carlos: Quick note, our primary constraints are latency under 150ms for 95th pctl on short prompts, and data residency — some of our dataset's PII needs to stay in EU.
[00:28] Priya: Great — that's exactly what we want to scope. Can you tell us about your current stack and how you expect to call the models?
[00:34] Ethan: We're a Python shop for backend inference, some TypeScript on the edge. We already use LangChain in a couple of experiments and LlamaIndex for doc retrieval. Ideally we'd like minimal refactor to plug into Redwood.
[00:48] Jordan: Cool. Redwood offers SDKs for Python and Node, plus a REST API. We also have example LangChain wrappers and a LlamaIndex connector — I'll share notebooks.
[00:56] Maya: How mature are those wrappers? Do they support streaming and tool calls? We've got user-facing streaming chat and also structured outputs for ranking.
[01:06] Priya: The LangChain/LLamaIndex adapters are production-ready; they support chunked streaming and structured outputs. There are edge cases with some community connector versions, but our examples are pinned to verified combos.
[01:20] Carlos: On deployment modes: what's the typical tradeoff? Hosted looks easiest but concerned about tail latency and multi-tenant noisy neighbors.
[01:28] Jordan: Exactly — hosted is fastest for time-to-value and scales automatically. For predictable latency and capacity we recommend Dedicated (reserved GPU pools). Private gives you VPC/on-prem control for compliance and data locality.
[01:39] Ethan: For dedicated, how does autoscaling behave? We might have spiky traffic during promotions — need bursts but want predictable cost.
[01:46] Priya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and burst capacity. You can set baseline throughput with committed capacity and allow burst buckets; we expose queueing/backpressure metrics in the console.
[01:56] Maya: And the networking side for Private — can we bring our own gateway or do you provide a proxy?
[02:03] Priya: Two patterns: 1) Redwood-managed gateway/proxy in your VPC which terminates traffic to the private control plane, or 2) a lightweight on-prem gateway image that you run — it handles auth, routing, and local caching (prefix/KV cache). Both support mTLS and integration with your load balancer.
[02:20] Carlos: That on-prem gateway — does it require inbound connectivity to Redwood? We have strict air-gap constraints for some customers.
[02:27] Priya: If fully air-gapped, we'd do an on-prem bundle with offline install and a customer-managed control plane; feature set is slightly different (no SaaS telemetry by default) but audit logs and local observability are included.
[02:39] Ethan: Observability — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency dashboards. Is that available?
[02:46] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and you can export traces to your observability pipeline (Datadog/Zipkin/OTel). We also give per-request metadata for sampling and correlation IDs.
[02:58] Maya: How do rate limits and quotas work? We want strict daily budgets for some internal teams, but unlimited for core product.
[03:06] Priya: We support tiered quotas and per-token and per-minute rate limits. For Dedicated/Private you can configure tenant-level quotas, burst policies, and prioritized routing. Hosted API has default rate limits which we can adjust for enterprise customers.
[03:20] Ethan: Any SDK-level helpers for handling 429s / retry backoff? We currently implement exponential backoff but sometimes lose requests.
[03:27] Priya: The SDK provides built-in retry with jitter and a transparent queue/backoff policy. For streaming responses, we surface partial payloads and a recoverable state for resumed requests.
[03:40] Carlos: Security — we need SOC 2 + SSO integration, and we'd prefer to use our KMS for key management.
[03:46] Jordan: We have SOC 2 Type II and integrate with customer KMS/HSM in Dedicated and Private modes. For Hosted we offer customer-managed keys via cloud KMS and bring-your-own-key options. SSO/SAML and RBAC are supported.
[03:58] Maya: Any concerns about model caching and retention? We can't have prompts logged for more than 30 days for some datasets.
[04:05] Priya: Retention policies are configurable. For Hosted we can set short retention and exclude sensitive payloads from logs. For Private you control retention locally.
[04:14] Ethan: We use LlamaIndex for dense retrieval — does Redwood expose vector DB connectors or do we keep vectors in our infra?
[04:21] Jordan: You can keep vectors in your infra and call Redwood for model scoring, or we integrate with hosted vector stores via connectors. Many customers run vector DBs (Pinecone/Weaviate) and call Redwood for embedding + reranking.
[04:34] Maya: Embeddings — we need deterministic embeddings across deployments. If we switch from hosted to dedicated later, will embedding outputs change?
[04:41] Priya: If you pin model versions and quantization profiles, behavior is consistent. Embedding drift can happen across model upgrades; we recommend pinning versions and running a small eval suite. Redwood Optimize suggests quantization/profile settings based on workload.
[04:55] Carlos: Performance: can we run a pilot with a 5k qps synthetic benchmark? We want to measure 95p latency for 32-token prompts.
[05:02] Jordan: Absolutely. For Hosted we can run a benchmark in our preview region; for Dedicated we can provision a reserved pool. We'll share benchmarking scripts and a spreadsheet to collect results.
[05:12] Ethan: About cost — what's the typical per-token difference between hosted and dedicated?
[05:18] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based with higher per-token unit cost but no fixed commit; Dedicated amortizes the GPU cost across committed tokens so unit cost is lower for sustained throughput. We'll send a modeled comparison based on your traffic profile.
[05:30] Maya: Also curious about LLM tool calling and structured outputs for ranking pipelines — can we enforce output schema?
[05:37] Priya: We support structured output constraints and function/tool calling; you can also use our output validators and post-process hooks. For strict schema enforcement we recommend using the function-calling mode plus a lightweight local validator.
[05:49] Carlos: Network egress — for Private, if we run gateway in EU region, will data leave region for model execution?
[05:56] Priya: No, for Private in a customer VPC the model execution happens in the configured region; data residency is maintained. For Hosted multi-region routing can be configured to keep EU traffic in EU regions.
[06:08] Maya: Any limits on model size or custom models? We have a fine-tuned T5 variant for ranking.
[06:15] Jordan: You can bring custom models. Dedicated and Private support custom model uploads/registry with versioning and rollouts. There are some constraints on quantization and GPU compatibility — Priya can follow up with specifics for your model.
[06:26] Priya: Note — for fine-tunes we usually recommend model packaging guidelines (hf format, KV cache compatibility). We'll run a quick compatibility check.
[06:36] Ethan: What about latency optimizations like continuous batching and KV cache warmup?
[06:41] Priya: Our serving runtime supports continuous batching, prefix/KV caching, and optimized kernels selected based on sequence length. We also have cache pre-warming APIs and hooks for warm start.
[06:52] Maya: For our use-case, user queries are short but we chain a retrieval step — so prefix caching and small-batch optimization are important.
[06:59] Jordan: Makes sense. We'll include recommended batch sizes and quantization profiles.
[07:05] Carlos: Can you show us an example of the LangChain integration flow? Like retriever -> LlamaIndex -> Redwood call?
[07:12] Priya: Sure. Example flow: LlamaIndex builds the index and returns candidate docs, you form a prompt template (we have templates), call Redwood via the Python SDK with a stream hook, and attach metadata for tracing. I'll send a sample notebook that wires this together.
[07:26] Maya: How do you handle multi-tenant tagging in logs so we can attribute cost to product lines?
[07:32] Jordan: We support per-request metadata tagging. Console has route-level cost breakdown and you can export to your billing system by tags.
[07:40] Ethan: Any gotchas with LangChain versions? We've had connector breakage when LangChain bumped APIs.
[07:46] Priya: Yes, we pin our examples to a tested LangChain release and maintain migration notes. For production we recommend pinning dependency versions and using Redwood's adapter shim to insulate minor changes.
[07:59] Carlos: Let's talk timeline — we want a pilot in the next 4 weeks with a POC team of 3. Is that reasonable?
[08:06] Jordan: That's reasonable. Steps: pricing and capacity proposal, security docs, then a technical deep dive to scope the Private/Dedicated pilot. After sign-off we provision Dedicated nodes or provide Private bundle.
[08:18] Maya: Helpful. Can you also include estimated onboarding time and a checklist of integrations (SSO, KMS, gateway)?
[08:24] Priya: Yes, we'll include an onboarding checklist and required network/infra changes.
[08:30] Jordan: Okay let's recap actions quickly — I'll send pricing and the hosted vs dedicated breakdown, Priya will prepare the Private deployment checklist and the LangChain notebook; Maya will share latency SLOs and prompt sets.
[08:42] Maya: Sounds good.
[08:44] Carlos: Thanks, looking forward to the deep dive.
[08:46] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up with calendar invites. Appreciate the time.
[08:50] Maya: Thanks everyone.
[08:52] End of call

Notes: transcript includes occasional mis-words from auto-transcription (e.g., 'LLamaIndex' sometimes 'Llama index' or 'llama index'). Some timestamps approximate speaker pauses. References: shared notebook link (link not included in transcript) and benchmark spreadsheet to be shared via email.
